title: A Follow-up Study of Mezagitamab in Adults With Chronic Primary Immune Thrombocytopenia
off: A Phase 3, Open-label, Multicenter Continuation Trial to Evaluate the Long-term Safety and Efficacy of Mezagitamab Subcutaneous Injection in Adults With Chronic Primary Immune Thrombocytopenia
summary:
Primary immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is a condition where the immune system mistakenly destroys platelets, which are cells that help stop bleeding. This leads to a lower number of platelets, making it easier to bruise or bleed. The main aim of this study is to check how safe mezagitamab is and how well it is tolerated by adults with chronic primary ITP, if given over a longer time. Other aims are to learn how effective treatment with mezagitamab is and how the body processes it (called pharmacokinetics or PK) over a longer time.

Participants of the following previous mezagitamab studies will be invited to join this continuation study: TAK-079-3002 and TAK-079-1004. In this continuation study, participants will receive mezagitamab when certain protocol criteria are met.

During the study, participants will visit their study clinic several times.
elig:
* Key Inclusion Criteria:

  1\. The participant has completed TAK-079-3002 (end of trial \[EOT\]) or TAK-079-1004 (EOT). Participants from TAK-079-1004 must have had a response to mezagitamab as demonstrated by meeting the criteria for "platelet response" specified for that trial during either the main study or open-label extension.
* Key Exclusion criteria:

For TAK-079-3002 participants:

1\. The participant has a history of severe allergic or anaphylactic reactions to recombinant proteins or excipients used in the mezagitamab formulation.

For TAK-079-1004 participants:

1. The participant has had any thrombotic or embolic event within 12 months before signing the ICF.
2. The participant has had a splenectomy within 3 months before signing the ICF.
3. The participant has active infection with hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), or human immunodeficiency virus (HIV).
4. History of malignancy (including myelodysplastic syndrome) within 5 years of signing the ICF, except for treated non-melanoma skin cancer or cervical carcinoma in situ.
5. In the opinion of the investigator, the participant has a serious medical or psychiatric illness that could potentially interfere with the completion of treatment according to this protocol.
6. The participant has received anti-cluster of differentiation (CD) 20 treatment within 12 months before screening and either of the following applies:

   1. The last dose was received within 6 months before screening.
   2. The last dose was received between 6 and 12 months before screening and the participant has a CD19+ count below the lower limit of normal.
7. The participant has received any monoclonal or polyclonal antibody for immunomodulation within 6 months before Visit 1.
8. The participant has been exposed to another investigational agent within 4 weeks or 5 half-lives, whichever is longer, before Visit 1.
9. The participant has used anticoagulants (for example, vitamin K antagonists, direct oral anticoagulants) within 3 weeks prior to Visit 1.

10 The participant has received a live or live-attenuated vaccine within 4 weeks prior to the first dose of trial treatment or has any live or live-attenuated vaccine planned during the trial.

11\. The participant has used the following immunosuppressive agents as specified prior to Visit 1: alkylating agents (for example, cyclophosphamide) within 8 weeks, vinca alkaloids (for example, vincristine) within 4 weeks, sulfones (for example, dapsone) within 3 weeks, antiproliferative agents: (for example, mycophenolate mofetil and azathioprine) within 2 weeks, and calcineurin inhibitors: (for example, cyclosporine) within 2 weeks.

12\. The participant has a history of severe allergic or anaphylactic reactions to recombinant proteins or excipients used in the mezagitamab formulation.

Other protocol defined inclusion/exclusion criteria may apply.

arms.d: Eligible participants who completed the TAK-079-3002 or TAK-079-1004 studies can receive on-demand treatment in this continuation study. The on-demand treatment course may be repeated as needed based on the pre-specified on-demand dosing criteria and investigator's clinical judgement.

x.titre: Étude de suivi du mézagitamab dans le PTI primaire chronique de l'adulte
x.question: Le mézagitamab est-il sûr et bien toléré lors d'une utilisation prolongée chez des adultes atteints de PTI primaire chronique ?
x.contexte:
Le purpura thrombopénique immunologique (PTI) primaire est une maladie auto-immune où le système immunitaire détruit les plaquettes et altère leur production, avec risque de saignement. Les formes chroniques nécessitent souvent plusieurs lignes de traitement (corticoïdes, agonistes de la TPO, rituximab, immunosuppresseurs, splénectomie), avec une efficacité inconstante.

Le mézagitamab (TAK-079) est un anticorps monoclonal anti-CD38 qui élimine les plasmocytes et plasmablastes, sources d'auto-anticorps, ainsi que d'autres cellules exprimant CD38. Il est en cours d'évaluation dans le PTI et d'autres maladies à médiation par des auto-anticorps.

Cette étude de phase 3, monobras et promue par Takeda, est une extension destinée aux participants ayant terminé les essais TAK-079-3002 ou TAK-079-1004. Les patients de l'essai 1004 doivent avoir présenté une réponse plaquettaire. Le traitement est administré à la demande lorsque les critères du protocole sont remplis, et peut être répété selon les besoins. L'objectif principal est la sécurité à long terme, sur environ 108 semaines.
x.interet: L'étude fournira des données de sécurité à long terme, essentielles pour juger la place d'un anti-CD38 dans le PTI chronique, et documentera l'intérêt d'un schéma de retraitement à la demande.
x.profil: Des adultes atteints de PTI primaire chronique ayant terminé les essais TAK-079-3002 ou TAK-079-1004 sur le mézagitamab.
inclusion: Fin de l'essai TAK-079-3002 ou de l'essai TAK-079-1004
Pour l'essai 1004 : réponse plaquettaire au mézagitamab pendant l'étude principale ou son extension
exclusion: Pour l'essai 3002 : antécédent de réaction allergique ou anaphylactique grave aux protéines recombinantes ou aux excipients
Pour l'essai 1004 : événement thrombotique ou embolique dans les 12 mois
Infection active par le VHB, le VHC ou le VIH
Tumeur maligne dans les 5 ans (sauf exceptions)
Maladie grave jugée incompatible, anti-CD20 récent

bras.traitement: Mézagitamab à la demande, cures répétables selon les critères du protocole ; dose non précisée

x.critere: Nombre de participants avec événements indésirables apparus sous traitement (graves ou entraînant l'arrêt définitif), jusqu'à environ 108 semaines
